summary.text: Alex Hakizimana is the Family First candidate for St Albans at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he was born to Burundian parents in the Congo (DRC), fled in 1997, lived for 12 years in a Tanzanian refugee camp and was resettled in Australia in 2009. He has worked as an interpreter since 2020 and in 2023 set up an NDIS service provider, which he directs.

summary.text: John Cowell is One Nation's candidate for St Albans at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in western Victoria and works in the construction industry. His party page says he moved to Melbourne's western suburbs in 2019 and has lived in the St Albans electorate with his family since 2023.

priorities.text: A fairer share of state investment for Melbourne's western suburbs
No more industrial waste sites, tips and data centres being placed in the west
Permanent closure of the Kealba landfill
Upgrading Taylors Road and building the Airport Rail link
Crime prevention, better roads and hospitals, and lower living costs

priorities.text: I’m a left-winger who thinks Labor needs to rein its spending in.

Longer opening hours at the Keilor Downs police station

summary.text: Kerry Janten is standing as an independent for St Albans at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. According to the campaign site, Janten has lived in the neighbouring Kororoit district for eight years and chose to run next door in St Albans. The site's main proposals are to scrap the rest of the Suburban Rail Loop, postpone the Melbourne Airport Rail link in favour of better airport buses, and retrofit inner-city public housing towers rather than rebuild them.

summary.text: Leanna Nguyen is the Victorian Socialists candidate for St Albans at the 2026 Victorian election. She says she has spent her whole life in the St Albans area. She has been active in anti-racism campaigns, including one that closed a gym in the western suburbs used for neo-Nazi recruitment, and has helped organise student protests over the war in Gaza.

prior_roles.role: Organiser of student protests for Palestine

priorities.text: I’ll fight for price controls on staple goods
A new state-owned bank offering lower mortgage rates to working-class households
Rent caps to make housing more affordable
A large expansion of public housing and an end to the privatisation of core services
More money for hospitals, schools and community centres

summary.text: Luận Walker is the West Party candidate for St Albans at the 2026 Victorian election. Born in Vietnam, he has worked as a youth-at-risk coordinator, as a pastor, and in rehabilitation programs at Ravenhall Correctional Centre, and the ABC lists him as a restaurant owner and the managing director of an aged care organisation. He was previously a Liberal Party member and was fourth on the Liberal ticket for Western Metropolitan Region in 2022.

occupation.text: Restaurant owner; managing director of an aged care organisation

prior_roles.role: Rehabilitation, pastoral care and multicultural engagement work at Ravenhall Correctional Centre

summary.text: Natalie Suleyman has been the Labor MP for St Albans since the seat was created in 2014. A former Brimbank councillor who was mayor three times, she was the first Muslim woman elected to the Victorian Parliament. She has been a minister since December 2022 and now holds Veterans, Small and Family Business, and Trade, Tourism and Investment. She is recontesting St Albans in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Trade, Tourism and Investment
Minister for Small and Family Business
Minister for Small Business and Employment
Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
Chair, Legal and Social Issues Committee

legal_and_integrity.text: A Victorian Ombudsman investigation into Brimbank City Council found that, as a councillor, she had improperly used her position, including directing that funding for a reserve be withdrawn after she lost a 2008 preselection, and that her account to the Ombudsman was an attempt to mislead.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: No action followed from the Local Government Inspectorate; the report contributed to the council's dismissal in 2009.

summary.text: Rob Dunstan is the Liberal candidate for St Albans at the 2026 Victorian election. He has been a police officer for about 30 years, and his campaign centres on crime in Melbourne's west. His party page also promotes the Liberals' proposed weekly toll cap of $50.

priorities.text: Reducing crime, backing his party's pledge of 3000 extra police and tougher sentencing
Lower living costs, including a $50 weekly cap on tolls

summary.text: Thuc Bao Huynh is the Greens candidate for St Albans at the 2026 Victorian election. A social policy academic, he calls himself a local from Melbourne's west. He stood for the Greens in the federal seat of Gorton in 2025, where Wikipedia lists him as Thuc Thuc Bao Huynh, with 10.8 per cent of first preferences.
